1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 25.11.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main),
Panchmahals at Godhra in MACP No.640 of 2010.

2. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellant - original claimant under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant-original claimant entitled to an amount of Rs.2,86,600/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
Thus, the Tribunal has not entertained the claim petition for an amount of Rs.10,50,000/- as total compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1

On 14.03.2010, the appellant was going as a Pedestrian nearby Godhra RTO Circle and at that time, at about 9:00 am, the respondent No.1 by driving his car bearing No. GJ-7-H-6283 in a negligent and rash manner dashed with the appellant.
After that, the appellant was rushed to the Hospital, whereby he has sustained permanent partial disablement.
3.2 Therefore, the appellant - original claimant had filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- with cost and interest against the respondents before the Tribunal.
3.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

4. This Court vide order dated 10.11.2014 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/763/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined original claimant and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned advocate Mr. MTM Hakim appearing for the appellant-original claimant, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimant and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

It is contended that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the appellant, pain, shock and suffering and loss of amenities of the appellant as well as prospective income of the appellant, and has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future prospects and grant of compensation under the various heads such as pain, shock and suffering and loss of amenities of life and actual loss of income.

5.1 It is further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the financial dependency of the family members and the Charansinh Dolatsinh Chauhan vs Shantilal Bhikhaji Bhill on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129053922/

The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.
Learned counsel therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation amount by reassessing the same in accordance with law.

6. Learned advocate Mr. G.C. Mazmudar appearing of the respondent No.3-Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/763/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record, awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.
7.

Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the record and proceedings and impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.

8. As regards the disability of the appellant is concerned, it appears from the disability certificate of the appellant produced on Exhibit-26 that the applicant has sustained 75% permanent partial disablement.
On behalf of the appellant, Dr. Jayesh Patel has been examined at Exhibit-25, who has issued the said disability certificate.

He has also been cross-examined by the learned advocate of the Insurance company and from the cross-examination, he has admitted that, as per the book of Dr.
R.M. Jhala, published for assessment of disability, if disability of lower extremity is assessed 75%, it will be assessed 30% as whole body.

Considering these facts, in the impugned judgment, the learned Tribunal rightly assessed 30% disability as whole body as just and proper and not required to interfere in the findings recorded in the impugned judgment.

9. So far as the income of the appellant is concerned, the appellant in his affidavit filed at Exhibit-24 stated that, at the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/763/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined time of incident, he was doing labour work of centering work and agriculture and thereby,
earning Rs. 4,000/- per month.
It appears from record that the applicant has not produced any income proof.
Hence, it is required to consider the notional income considering the type of work and also considering the year of the incident.
The learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the work of the petitioner.
It appears that appellant is a skilled worker and learned Tribunal ought to have assessed monthly income of Rs. 4,000/-.

Hence, it is required to assess the monthly income as Rs. 4,000/- of the appellant at the time of incident in the year 2010 and is required to be considered and applied while calculating the compensation.

Considering the nature of his work and injury sustained, and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the appellant - original claimant as 29 years, as accepted by the Tribunal by considering the evidence on record, 40% amount can be considered towards the future prospects of the appellant - original claimant.

11.

So far as the compensation under the other heads such as pain, shock and suffering and special diet, attendant charges and transportation are concerned, the Tribunal has awarded Rs. 25,000/-
towards pain, shock and suffering and Rs.6000/- towards special diet, attendance charges and transportation, etc., which is on a much lower side considering the injuries sustained by the appellant - original claimant due to which he has suffered 30% disability and suffered Paraplegia,
whereby lower portion of his body has suffered permanent disability, as coming out from the disability certificate at Exhibit-26 and deposition of the Doctor, who examined him, at Exhibit-25.
Therefore, considering the facts of the case, nature of injuries, medical treatment and physical pain and the emotional trauma endured by the appellant, who was only a Pedestrian, a substantial enhancement under the abovementioned heads are deserves to be enhanced.

In light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu Deo Yadav v. Naresh Kumar and ors., reported in AIR 2020 SC 4424, towards the Pain, Shock and Suffering endured by the appellant and Loss of Amenities Rs.3,00,000/- is required to be considered along with Rs. 15,000/- towards special diet,
attendance charges and transportation, etc.
12.

Hence, under the head of actual loss of income, Rs.12,000/- (Rs. 4,000 x 3)

15. Let, the aforesaid amount be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the present order.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to release and disburse the entire award amount in favour of the original claimant, after due verification as per the original judgment and award.

16. Let, such exercise be undertaken by the Tribunal strictly in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard; preferably within a period of two weeks from deposit of such amount.
